definition: GPT-J or GPT-J-6B is an open-source large language model (LLM) developed by EleutherAI in 2021.
details: As the name suggests, it is a generative pre-trained transformer model designed to produce human-like text that continues from a prompt. The optional "6B" in the name refers to the fact that it has 6 billion parameters. The model is available on GitHub, but the web interface no longer communicates with the model. Development stopped in 2021.

explainer.lead: GPT-J is an open-source language model from EleutherAI that continues a written prompt with human-like text. Its 6 billion parameters put the “6B” in its alternative name, GPT-J-6B.

tiers.eli5: GPT-J is like a very large autocomplete: you give it the start of a sentence, and it tries to write what might come next. It was shared openly so other people could use it, rather than being kept behind a single company’s service.
tiers.practitioner: GPT-J-6B takes a text prompt and generates a continuation using a 6-billion-parameter transformer. The model is available on GitHub, but development stopped in 2021 and the web interface no longer communicates with it, so it should not be treated as an actively maintained service.
tiers.paperLevel: GPT-J-6B is a generative pre-trained transformer defining a text-continuation mapping: prompt -> generated text, with approximately 6 billion learned parameters. It was developed by EleutherAI in 2021; development stopped that year, and its web interface is no longer functional.

explainer.example: Given the prompt “The cat sat on the”, GPT-J could generate a continuation such as “windowsill and watched the birds.” The exact wording is generated by the model rather than fixed in advance.

explainer.lineage: GPT-J is also called GPT-J-6B because it has 6 billion parameters. Development stopped in 2021.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPT-J made a 6-billion-parameter generative language model available as open source, allowing people to obtain a model for prompt-based text generation.
